Tomorrow, I’ll be on the ground at SXSW with the ElevenLabs team to showcase 11 Voices - a docuseries following 11 people from around the world living with conditions like ALS and cerebral palsy, who used our technology to regain their voices. We started our Impact work three years ago, almost exactly at the same time we launched our first product at ElevenLabs. One of the first people we worked with was Lori Cohen, a lawyer who returned to the courtroom with an AI voice and went on to inspire many others through her powerful speeches. Since then, we’ve partnered with 500 non-profits and have been honoured to help 7,000 people get their voices back. This is part of our broader 1 Million Voices initiative - a global partnerships programme we launched at ElevenLabs to provide free voice restoration for all people with permanent voice loss. Tomorrow, we will also be joined by Rebecca Gayheart Dane to reflect on what this work can mean on a deeply personal level. Eric Dane was one of the people we had the privilege to work with as ALS progressed and he began losing his voice. In his final weeks, we helped him preserve and restore it, and he became a strong supporter of this mission and the importance of making this technology available to others. It is deeply meaningful to have Rebecca with us as part of this conversation, alongside Yvonne, who has worked closely with us over past years and has been an incredible partner in bringing this technology to life. Thank you as well to everyone who helped bring 11 Voices to life behind the scenes - our partners and team: Dustin, Sophia, Gabi, Richard. …more

Artificial intelligence is the key technology of our time. AI determines competitiveness, technological performance, and Europe’s digital sovereignty. That is why Deutsche Telekom has consistently invested in hashtag #AI for years, ensuring that the latest technologies are available in our networks. We are showcasing this commitment this week at the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona. I welcomed Federal Minister for Digital Affairs Karsten Wildberger and presented our latest innovations to him. To name just a few: • Magenta AI Call Assistant With our AI assistant, we are demonstrating our vision of AI-supported phone calls of the future. AI becomes an integral part of the conversation—in real time, without additional apps or hardware. Simply say “Hey Magenta” to activate the AI during a call. It translates live, summarizes conversations, and answers questions. Developed in collaboration with ElevenLabs and available later this year. • MINDR – the path to a self-healing network With MINDR, we are taking the next step toward an autonomous network. The multi-agent system developed together with Google Cloud continuously monitors our network, detects anomalies or rising utilization at an early stage—before customers even notice anything. Our goal: an intelligent, predictive, self-healing network. • Security in the age of AI and deepfakes Digital sovereignty requires security – including verified digital identities for people and AI systems. At hashtag #MWC, we are presenting a new security concept to protect automated, sensitive business processes. And with a deepfake exhibit, we are making real attack scenarios tangible. AI is changing everything. Communication. Networks. Processes. Our ambition is clear: We are shaping this transformation – responsibly, innovatively, and from Europe. And this requires connectivity – everywhere. We are complementing our mobile network with satellite-based direct connectivity and closing coverage gaps. In partnership with hashtag #Starlink, we are also providing service in regions where it is difficult to deploy mobile sites – for example in high mountain areas or nature reserves. The launch is planned for early 2028 in several European Telekom markets, including Germany. For a digital Europe that confidently charts its own course. hashtag #digitalesouveränität hashtag #telekom hashtag #europa hashtag #ki hashtag #künstlicheintelligenz Abdu Mudesir Rodrigo Diehl Dr. Ferri Abolhassan Mati Staniszewski …more

Today, we’re expanding our partnership with Deutsche Telekom. What’s exciting is that, for the first time, we’re bringing an AI voice assistant directly into the experience people already use every day - the network. It can act as an assistant, a real-time translator, and more. Access to intelligence usually means downloading a new app, visiting a new website, or relearning a new interface. Here, we’re doing it in the most natural way - through voice - and in the flow of how you already communicate with another person - a phone call. 2 months ago we announced our work together to bring voice agents into DT's customer service. Now we are expanding - later this year, existing Deutsche Telekom subscribers, when calling another person, will be able to say “Hey Magenta” during that conversation and instantly get an AI agent that can help both of you out - agent that speaks naturally, understands context & has access to knowledge, can translate and act on your behalf. And earlier today we demoed it live during Mobile World Congress with Abdu Mudesir. That opens up so many new behaviours: - Magenta as an AI call assistant, helping in real time with information and actions. For example if you need check your calendar, get a suggestion for a dinner place while speaking, pull up an email you send a while back - Magenta as a real-time translator, help finally break down the language barrier. You don't speak the language - no problem - Magenta will translate it with you in real-time. - Magenta summarizing your call afterwards, sending follow-ups, or creating an invite - Magenta helping you before a call - taking a call with the person calling to gather more context before passing it over to you! I am very excited about this partnership between Telekom team & ElevenLabs - truly bringing new experiences, in the best possible way! Thanks for the incredible partnership! …more

A first for the industry - voice agents built with ElevenLabs can now be covered by proper insurance. Today, ElevenLabs becomes the first company to secure insurance for AI voice agents, backed by AIUC-1 certification. One of the biggest barriers to deploying agents at scale is trust and reliability. Every enterprise deployment depends on systems holding up across countless situations - but you still need coverage for edge cases if something goes wrong. AIUC-1 is a leading third-party standard for AI safety, security, and reliability, developed with Fortune 500 security and risk leaders. Earning it requires passing 5,000+ adversarial simulations across security vulnerabilities, data privacy, hallucinations, and safety. It’s a rigorous technical bar. For companies building on ElevenAgents, it unlocks three things: - Validate agent safety - quantify AI risk before it reaches your customers - Deploy faster - fast-track internal security reviews with third-party validation - Insure your agents - AIUC-1 is the only certification that creates the risk profile insurers need to underwrite AI systems Companies building on ElevenAgents are already up to 75% of the way to certification and can achieve it in weeks, thanks to built-in protections. …more

A few reflections from Davos and WEF - a rare chance to meet so many incredible people in person. I’ll admit I went in sceptical: how much is PR, how much is real value? We tend to avoid talking and prefer building. But one thing is clear - it’s a brilliant forcing function. Everyone is in one place, and you can compress what normally takes weeks into days. What stood out to me as a first-timer: - It’s a great equaliser. Everyone walks the same promenade - presidents, CEOs, founders, teams - and you keep running into people in a way that doesn’t happen anywhere else. The formal meetings matter, but the informal collisions are where you often learn something you wouldn’t otherwise. For next time: leave more room for impromptu meetings. - With preparation, it can be one of the most productive weeks of the year for in-person meetings. Thanks to amazing work from Franek (in the picture!), we ran a packed schedule - 20+ 1:1 meetings in four days - from Sony, through Allegro to Verizon. We went deep on how conversational agents and voice can elevate customer experience, marketing, and more - and, just as importantly, what’s top of mind for leaders going into the year ahead. We also got some deals and projects started - one captured exactly at 11:11. For next time: preparation and follow-up make all the difference - leave extra time in evening for immediate follow-ups! - You get to learn from the best during the roundtables and panels. You do feel like an impostor for a minute sitting next to legends - which is probably a good sign. From dropping into Bloomberg just before Demis Hassabis slot, to conversations with Anne Neuberger and Eric Schmidt, to the WEF panel alongside some of Europe’s largest companies - it was energising. It was also fun to share what’s working at ElevenLabs: how you can build from Europe and still compete (and win!) globally, and how we try to work with customers - go deep, partner, and prove value quickly. For next time: take more photos - some of these moments are surreal (a few that I did attached below). - It can feel like two conferences happening at once. Global geopolitics on one track, and enterprise transformation on the other - and this year the contrast felt sharp. Greenland, Ukraine, Europe’s regulatory push - while, in the next room, people are obsessing over how AI is changing the way companies operate. What stuck with me most is the incredible energy at the Polish House during the panel, the conversations with European regulators, and time with the US and UK delegations. The two tracks are intertwined - and given the stakes, it’s a good reminder to zoom out once in a while: not just to build, but to help shape the conditions that let building happen. For next time: spend more time on intersection between AI & public sector. As valuable as it was to spend time with so many people in one place, I’m glad to now spent a a few days with my co-founder, Piotr and the team - turning this week into product, shipped. …more
